findings.title: UsernameForm re-auth with passkeys but no passkey registered shows the username form
findings.body: When conditional passkeys are enabled for the realm and context.getUser() != null, the auto-skip is bypassed for every user, not just those who have a passkey. A re-authenticating user with no passkey is forced through the username form again. Because USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is not set in this path, the form may offer a different username instead of re-authenticating the current user. The previous behaviour (skip the form) is lost for non-passkey users. The existing tests do not cover this case for UsernameForm.

findings.title: Conditional passkey UI enabled in re-authentication even if the user has no passkey
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) only checks that passkeys are enabled and the user is non-null. During re-authentication, the webauthn form and conditional UI are therefore rendered for users with no registered passkey. The WebAuthn authenticator list is deliberately hidden (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators returns false), so nothing narrows the prompt to this user's credentials. Discoverable credentials of a different user could be offered. A later mismatch is rejected only by the different-user check, which gives a confusing error.

findings.title: Negative assertion wrapped in try/catch(Exception) is ineffective
findings.body: fail(...) throws AssertionError, which is an Error and not an Exception, so it is not swallowed. The real flaw is that findElement throws NoSuchElementException, so the assertThat(..., nullValue()) line is never reached when the element is absent. Any other Exception, such as a driver or timeout error, also silently passes the test. Use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) or findElements(...).isEmpty() instead.
